_comment: Copy this file to webapp_config.json (gitignored) or let the webapp create it on the first 'Save defaults' tap. All keys are optional — missing keys fall back to the defaults in src/webapp_config.py.
_comment_auth_token: Empty string = auth gate OFF (the default). Run scripts/gen_token.py to generate a strong token; the webapp will then require Authorization: Bearer <token> on every API call from non-loopback callers.
_comment_auth_password: Optional companion to auth_token: when set, a fresh device with no token shows a login overlay; entering the password swaps it for the bearer token. Set/clear via scripts/set_password.py. Failed attempts are logged to webapp/auth.log.
_comment_projects_dir: Master folder whose direct child directories the Coding tab lists as launchable projects. Defaults to the parent of this repo (E:\automation\... by default).
_comment_projects_ignore: gitignore-style patterns: directory names under projects_dir to hide from the Coding tab. Matched case-insensitively against the bare folder name; * and ? globs are honoured (e.g. 'archive', '*-old'). VCS/build dirs (.git, .venv, node_modules, ...) are always skipped regardless.
_comment_coding_favorites: Project ids (scanner slugs of the folder name) starred as favorites in the Coding tab (issue #250). Favorites sort to the top of the project list, and the '★ Favorites' header toggle filters the list to only these. Managed by tapping the per-tile star — you don't normally hand-edit this. Stored here, like projects_ignore, so the feature needs no extra file.
_comment_coding_hidden_agents: Coding-row launch buttons to hide (issue #666): agent ids from src/agents.py plus the pseudo-id 'github' for the repo-issues button (the id predates the GitLab move — kept for config compatibility; the visible label says 'Repository issues'). Managed by the 'Visible agents' switches in the Coding options card — you don't normally hand-edit this. It is a *hidden* list, not a visible one, so a newly registered agent shows up by default. Hiding only trims the project row; a running session still shows its agent in the sessions list and on the Board.
_comment_sessions_state_file: The sessions-state.json written by fleet-config-lite's session_state Copilot hook — the Board reads it for agent-aware session status (working / needs-you / ...). Defaults to ~/.copilot/hooks/state/sessions-state.json. Absent/corrupt/stale degrades to unknown status, never an error.
_comment_apps_scan_root: Where the Apps tab scans recursively for launcher *.bat files. Defaults to the same parent as projects_dir.
_comment_team_os_dir: Root of the team-os checkout the Team OS tab surfaces (issue #102). Skills live at <team_os_dir>/.claude/skills, identity at <team_os_dir>/identity. Defaults to the sibling ../team-os; when the skills dir doesn't exist the tab shows disabled, the same way the Coding tab handles a missing projects_dir. The private-content browser (context/memory/examples/conversations) is gated like the live terminal: Tailscale-only, refused over the Cloudflare tunnel, passkey-required.
_comment_copilot_flags: GitHub Copilot CLI (copilot) launch settings, set from the Coding options card. copilot_models is the list of model ids offered in the UI pickers — read-only from the UI, edit it here (explicit ids are tenant-gated; an unavailable id errors visibly in the PTY). copilot_model is the persisted --model value (empty or 'default' = let Copilot pick auto); copilot_skip_permissions is the --allow-all switch; copilot_autopilot maps to --autopilot; copilot_context to --context ('', 'default' or 'long_context'; empty = omit); copilot_effort to --effort ('', none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max; empty = omit — and it is only ever passed alongside an explicit model, because the auto model rejects --effort).
_comment_session_host_port: Loopback port the PTY session-host binds. Never network-reachable; the webapp proxies to it. Must differ from 'port'.
_comment_tailnet_allowlist: Extra IPs / CIDRs allowed to reach the interactive terminal endpoints, on top of loopback + the Tailscale CGNAT range 100.64.0.0/10. Leave empty unless you need LAN access.
_comment_show_local_window: When true (default), launching a session from the phone also opens an interactive terminal window for it on the PC. It connects over loopback so input works from both the phone and the PC.
_comment_terminal_history_lines: Bounded scrollback for full-screen agent sessions — how many lines of history the session-host retains and replays on a (re)connect (issue #435 follow-up). Settings-tab configurable. Default 10000 is evidence-based (see src/vt_snapshot.py); bounds are 200-50000.
_comment_webauthn: Passkey gate for the interactive terminal. webauthn_rp_id is the bare tailnet hostname (e.g. 'pc.tailnet.ts.net'); webauthn_origin is the full https origin the phone connects to (e.g. 'https://pc.tailnet.ts.net:8465'). Leave both empty to disable the passkey gate.
_comment_notifications: Jobs-tab failure notifications (issue #66). Set both pushover_api_token + pushover_user_key and flip notify_on_failure: true to start receiving a push per failed run. notify_failure_streak: N also fires when N consecutive failures stack up (0 = disabled).
_comment_telegram: Per-job Telegram failure alerts (issue #597), via the vendored src/notify Telegram primitive. Set both telegram_bot_token + telegram_chat_id here, then flip the 'Alert to Telegram if failed' toggle on individual jobs in the Jobs tab edit dialog. Unlike notify_on_failure above (global, Pushover, fires for every job), this channel is opt-in per job so the shared Telegram chat isn't spammed by every failure.
_comment_jobs_coverage: Missed-fire coverage for scheduled jobs (issue #697). jobs_coverage_interval_minutes is how often the webapp re-scans every scheduled job for a missing/disabled \AppLauncher\ Task Scheduler entry or an elapsed slot that produced no run record; 0 disables the background tick (the Jobs-tab '⚠ not firing' badge still computes on poll). On by default because it pushes nothing on its own — alerts route through the two opt-in gates above (notify_on_failure for Pushover, a job's alert_on_failure for Telegram). See docs/jobs-tab.md.
_comment_secrets: One gitignored place for job secret values (issues #73, #72). A job's webhook.secret and any Job.env value can be a literal string or a '$secret:<key>' reference resolved against this dict at fire time, so a rotated credential lives here instead of jobs.json. Example: {"gh_key": "whsec_..."} then a job sets webhook.secret to "$secret:gh_key", or env to {"API_KEY": "$secret:gh_key"}. The legacy 'webhook_secrets' key still loads. See docs/jobs-tab.md.
_comment_api_tokens: Scoped API bearer tokens (issue #72), minted/revoked from the Settings tab — don't hand-edit. Each record stores only a salted SHA-256 hash of the token plus its scope ('*' or {"jobs": [ids]}); a job-scoped token can only call POST /api/jobs/<id>/run for its allowed jobs, so it is safe to bake into a Stream Deck button URL. The legacy auth_token keeps working unchanged.
_comment_gitlab: Board tab data source (Phase 5): gitlab_group is the GitLab group (subgroups included) whose projects the Board's glab queries span — empty keeps the panel dormant with a Settings hint. gitlab_host targets a self-hosted instance via glab's GITLAB_HOST env var; empty = glab's default context.
